variables.name: aAxis
variables.meaning: declarative axis and axis-view record count

variables.name: nDatum
variables.meaning: datums inspected by the Chart-owned definition reconciliation

contract.proof: Vue retains one record per low-cardinality coordinate, axis, layer, view, navigation, or control declaration and coalesces all touches in one nextTick publication. High-cardinality arrays remain opaque props; Chart owns datum validation and model reconciliation.
contract.adversarialWitness: Replacing a maximum-size layer array causes one declaration publication, a record scan bounded by axes plus layers, and no datum-sized Vue registry.

fullScan.rationale: Chart may inspect submitted datums to validate identity, resolve automatic domains, and reconcile packed owners; the Vue bridge does not traverse them.

contract.proof: Provider and Root each retain one controller snapshot subscription. Selector composables derive shallow values from that snapshot and publish only when their equality predicate changes; layer and axis scans are bounded by the public Chart ceilings.
contract.adversarialWitness: A model replacement changes every selected layer and axis while every mounted selector uses a comparator that reports inequality.

fullScan.rationale: Selectors may scan bounded definition metadata but cannot inspect datum arrays or materialize model data.

variables.name: n
variables.meaning: canonical tree nodes bounding selection, expansion and explicit configuration admission

contract.proof: Core and the Native controller own all checked aggregation and identity reconciliation. Vue shallow-publishes accepted snapshots, borrows Core selection/expansion membership directly, and projects only its mounted part ports. Tree construction occurs only for explicit configuration generations; Host/KeepAlive and root replacement reuse the accepted controller and O(m) presentation binding work.
contract.adversarialWitness: SSR hierarchy, refused controlled proposals, hidden/unmounted descendants, structural focus replacement, retained input getter counters during Host/KeepAlive suspension, root element replacement and zero Native listeners after unmount.

fullScan.rationale: Explicit structural/policy generations admit a new tree through Core. An accepted snapshot updates m mounted ports; suspension never reconstructs the node domain.

contract.proof: Vue delegates the explicit prop-replacement boundary to Core collection reconciliation and retains only the resulting controller snapshot.
contract.adversarialWitness: A disjoint equal-size prop replacement invalidates selection and current while visiting every external option once.

fullScan.rationale: External option replacement requires validation; ordinary controller events bypass this path.

variables.name: r
variables.meaning: mounted GridCell, ListboxItem, MenuItem, and MenuSubContent identity consumers
variables.ceiling: the owning collection's mounted item ceiling

variables.name: j
variables.meaning: mounted identities whose item-local projected state changes in the current publication
variables.ceiling: changed cursor/highlight identities plus selection, disabled-item, or menu-path deltas

variables.name: h
variables.meaning: Menu open-path depth inspected while publishing an open-path snapshot

variables.name: s
variables.meaning: Listbox selection identities inspected when the canonical selection reference actually changes

resources.cacheEntries: 0 retained item invalidation entries after each synchronous publication

assumptions: Core/domain controllers remain the semantic owner and DOM remains the host-projection owner; Vue stores only transient reactive key pulses rather than copied collection state.
Unchanged Listbox selection state is structurally shared, so a cursor-only transition sets s to zero and does not scan the selected domain.

A consumer that explicitly reads a changed root-wide slot property intentionally subscribes to that root property; the item-local guarantee applies to consumers that depend only on item-local projection fields.
Root disabled changes are genuinely global and invalidate r mounted identities through the shared root scalar rather than an item-domain sweep.
deterministicWork: At both 1000 and 4000 mounted identities, one ordinary cursor/highlight move executes exactly two consumer item slots in Grid, Listbox, and Menu.
Listbox selection publication invalidates only identities in the selection symmetric difference; hidden native option state is synchronized only for those changed identities.
Menu open-path publication compares path membership and invalidates only the symmetric path delta, while each MenuSubContent subscribes to its own parent identity key.

Item consumers subscribe to reactive Map keys through ordinary render dependency tracking; prop identity reuse, unmount, and remount rely on Vue effect dependency cleanup and retain no historical item token.
contract.resourceRationale: The Vue bridge uses one shallow-reactive Map per root as a transient keyed invalidation channel. Each pulse sets and deletes one key synchronously, leaving no retained identity entry; Vue owns O(r) render-effect subscriptions and releases them with component effects.
contract.proof: Root bridges mutate stable shallow-reactive public slot projections without replacing an aggregate computed object. Item-local getters read one reactive identity key and then canonical current state through non-aggregate accessors. Publishers pulse old/new cursor IDs, selection deltas, disabled-item deltas, or Menu open-path deltas; unrelated item effects are not scheduled.
contract.adversarialWitness: Mount 4000 Grid, Listbox, and Menu items, reset consumer slot counters after settlement, then move the cursor/highlight once. Each family must report exactly two consumer slot executions independent of r. Reuse identities, remove/remount consumers, and apply controlled or disabled-item changes to verify reactive-key dependency cleanup and targeted invalidation.

fullScan.rationale: Ordinary item-state publication must not scan or invalidate all mounted identities. Domain replacement and genuinely global root-disabled changes are explicit owner-reconfiguration branches outside this ordinary publication contract.

variables.name: sForm
variables.meaning: active subscribers on the form channel

variables.name: sField
variables.meaning: active subscribers for one field identifier

contract.proof: Each composable owns one shallowRef and one DOM Form selector subscription; field selectors bind directly to the field-ID channel and all reconnect cleanup uses one retained disposer.
contract.adversarialWitness: A field update with unrelated field subscribers must invoke only the changed field channel and form selectors whose selected value changes.

fullScan.rationale: The Vue bridge neither scans FormState.fields nor materializes the complete state projection.

variables.name: j
variables.meaning: cells whose projected cursor, selection, or item-disabled state changes
variables.ceiling: at most four distinct IDs for an ordinary cursor/selection transition

resources.cacheEntries: one registered primitive ID and one ref-counted Vue invalidation token per mounted identity

assumptions: Core and DOM own transitions and host attributes. The rows and root policies are stable during ordinary interaction.
Ordinary root state publication mutates a stable property-granular slot object and invalidates only identity channels whose item-local projection changed.
Construction and explicit owner reconfiguration may scan the domain, discover mounted parts, or invalidate all mounted identities when a genuinely global item state such as root disabled changes.
deterministicWork: At 1000 and 4000 mounted cells, initial registration writes exactly r gridcell roles.
At 1000 and 4000 mounted cells, one ArrowRight cursor transition executes exactly two GridCell consumer slots: the previous and next cursor identities.
Navigation, selection and a distant click perform zero part-discovery queries and zero static role rewrites; each tested settled transition writes at most 32 cell attributes.
Per-cell refs register identity and disabled changes, release the old ID on reuse, and release host ownership plus the Vue projection channel on unmount.
contract.resourceRationale: Mounted component subscriptions and identity channels are O(r). Ordinary item-local publication is O(j) and retains no historical identity entries; connection setup and explicit global reconfiguration are the only r-sized branches.
contract.proof: GridRoot publishes canonical scalar changes into one stable shallow-reactive root slot projection and invalidates previous/new identity channels without calling refreshParts. GridCell local getters subscribe to only their identity token while root-wide public getters remain lazy reactive dependencies. Discovery is restricted to connection setup and stable cell refs feed single-cell registration into the DOM owner.
contract.adversarialWitness: Mount 4000 cells, move the cursor by one cell, and count consumer slot executions separately from DOM writes. Exactly the old/new cell slots execute while part discovery remains zero. Then exercise controlled-state combinations, disabled changes, reused IDs, removal/remount, read-only and disabled gates, edit callbacks and unmount cleanup.

fullScan.rationale: Construction, domain replacement, and genuinely global item-state changes may touch r mounted cells. Ordinary cursor/selection publication does not take that branch and may not execute unrelated GridCell consumer slots.

resources.subscriptions: at most one Vue watch per adopted component

contract.proof: Resolution iteratively follows one component root at each level and stops at an exposed Element channel or native root. Each Primitive retains one shallow Element ref and at most one explicit watch; replacement stops the prior watch, and unmount clears it and the ref. Native children allocate no watch. Public exposure is projected outside setup and retains only the cleared ref.
contract.adversarialWitness: A 32-component delegation chain counts linear production subTree reads. Exposed/native root replacement, null availability, unmount and saved public exposure GC exercise retirement, including nested Fragment adoption.
deterministicWork: Component-root reads stay within twice the mounted chain depth plus fixed overhead.
Native children have no watch; adopted component replacement owns at most one watch and retired exposure changes trigger no resolver reads.

fullScan.rationale: No DOM descendant search, sibling scan or slot re-execution is used to resolve an adopted component.

resources.cacheEntries: one issued frame and one active operation

contract.proof: Snapshot admission reads one native value and fixed offsets, reuses the single issued frame for an unchanged connection/revision, and borrows canonical Core text/selection. A replacement dispatches one existing DOM/Core transition; Vue does not calculate replacement output again. Existing controlled watch/nextTick settlement records exact acceptance and final connection/revision. One busy operation cell admits no pending queue; unmount clears the frame and action callbacks.
deterministicWork: one native value read per snapshot call at100000 code units
unchanged reads reuse one issued object
a second pending edit is rejected before dispatch
contract.resourceRationale: One frame and one pending operation retain existing immutable text/proposal references; settlement waits only the existing Vue flush, not external work. Held public methods capture a cleared mutable port; returned snapshots do not reference the field/native owner.
contract.adversarialWitness: Large unchanged reads, foreign/stale/invalid range rejection, controlled acceptance/refusal/transformation, explicit lazy commit, superseding native input and reconnect, callback-driven unmount, and held methods/results with collected native/caller graphs.

fullScan.rationale: Native value materialization/equality and the existing Core immutable replacement may process the owned source/output and inserted text; Vue adds no independent text scan or duplicate replacement calculation.

variables.name: n
variables.meaning: native text code units read for snapshot admission

contract.proof: One existing native snapshot admission precedes the Core canonical query projection. Vue adds only a result wrapper pairing bounded query/range with the field-issued snapshot; it neither parses text nor constructs another state. Native materialization/equality may cost O(n). The returned snapshot borrows n source code units explicitly.
deterministicWork: existing snapshot native read and identity witness
contract.resourceRationale: No query cache or provider work is started. Optional snapshotChange observers share one coalesced nextTick callback with mounted retirement checks; fields without a listener schedule none. No callback captures a text/proposal argument. The existing revocable action port is cleared on unmount; returned query data contains no native/instance references. Future provider requests must not retain the full snapshot.
contract.adversarialWitness: Real field query-to-replacement acceptance, old range refusal after selection, no query during IME, invalid policy reporting and held query method after unmount/GC.

fullScan.rationale: Only the existing native text getter/equality boundary may process n; semantic query inspection is delegated to the bounded Core owner.

variables.name: n
variables.ceiling: current Core queue length and configured visible limit

assumptions: Core/DOM owns canonical queue/countdown state; Vue owns only shallow publication and exit presentation.
Map membership is expected constant time; native element lookup borrows the existing DOM registration owner.
Viewport-less publication retains only active items; no pending function history or unrendered exit rows.
ceilings: One active ID view per changed item generation, replacing the prior active-ID Set; no additional active registry.
Repeated identical native state publication is O(1); unchanged item arrays share membership and ordered rows.
Each row reads the current active/exit view with O(1) lookup, not a full-array search.
deterministicWork: Actual mounted 32/128-row tick publication performs zero per-row Array.find predicate visits.
A reactive label change preserves published item-array and native countdown callback identity.
Ten viewport-less pushes retain only the configured three active items, including after viewport detach.
contract.resourceRationale: One native actor remains across viewport/config changes. A clearable command cell and data-only computed refs do not retain a disposed provider or DOM. Registered presence exits use the existing exit Map; terminal disposal clears it and destroys the facade before late calls can run.
contract.proof: Refresh returns on identical native state and reuses membership when items are shared. Changed items build one ID Map, reconcile registered exits and materialize one ordered view. Root computeds query this view directly. The detached actor has no native clock/resources and respects Core queue limits.
contract.adversarialWitness: Viewport replacement/absence, reactive labels/policies, concurrent exits/reorder/reactivation, large mounted row views, saved commands after teardown and explicit-GC input/root collection.

fullScan.rationale: Changed active/exit generation requires one shallow ordered publication; per-row and duplicate same-state scans are not needed.

variables.name: n
variables.meaning: canonical source nodes and explicit admission/submission output

variables.name: q
variables.meaning: Native buffered Unicode query code points

variables.name: c
variables.meaning: Native normalized text output visited by typeahead
variables.ceiling: caller output over maxScan-admitted pane items

contract.proof: One Native controller owns both panes and portable atomic membership. Vue shallow-publishes accepted snapshots and borrows Core Sequences/Selection; it adds no topology or selected index. Explicit immutable source/policy replacement re-admits through Core, while Host/KeepAlive and element replacement only reconnect presentation. Cached option output encodes target membership in one render-owned hidden select; one Form participant borrows existing metadata/default/reset owners. Attachment/reset nextTick tasks coalesce and cancel. Unmount retires public method ports before disconnect/dispose and clears registrations; held methods cannot retain component roots/hooks.
contract.adversarialWitness: No-DOM SSR, controlled refusal/complete acceptance, source pruning, nested native controls, assigned membership versus temporary pane selection, Form reset/defaults, Host/KeepAlive six-listener churn with no source rereads or accepted ARIA loss, replaced/unmounted target, acquired-listener cleanup after caller eligibility failure and held-method explicit-GC collection.

fullScan.rationale: Explicit source/config admission and complete slot/submission output visit n; attachment visits mounted m. Ordinary controls and Host/KeepAlive do not rebuild the portable owner.

variables.name: n
variables.meaning: source tree nodes bounding explicit selection/topology admission and submission options

variables.name: m
variables.meaning: mounted tree item and disclosure ports

contract.proof: One SSR-created Native controller owns Core selection/query/expansion. Vue publishes immutable snapshots through shallowRef and borrows Core membership without rebuilding selected Sets. Explicit topology/policy replacement uses existing Tree and collection admission; Host/KeepAlive and element replacement only reattach presentation. One cached native-select vnode depends on selected owner/topology, not every cursor/query revision. Shared cancellable next-tick tasks own attachment/reset; unmount retires them, detaches Native work and disposes the controller. Core alone repairs uncontrolled hidden cursors.
contract.adversarialWitness: SSR with initial selected options and no transport; controlled refusal/acceptance, stale responses with later query acceptance, live IME through unrelated render, old requests after source replacement, Host/KeepAlive listener churn and exactly one Form submission owner/reset.

fullScan.rationale: Explicit source generations and native submission option output may visit n. Ordinary Native projection visits m mounted parts. Query results do not rebuild the source controller or selected owner.

variables.name: rRepair
variables.meaning: rows whose aggregate extent must be recomputed

variables.name: cLane
variables.ceiling: lanePolicy fixed count or responsive maxCount

assumptions: collection identity and changed-value windows come from the Virtual-owned projection
contract.proof: An unchanged effective width does not change viewportWidth and therefore schedules no Grid geometry repair. Value-only changes recompute only the contiguous affected row window. Fixed-size structural changes patch the dense identity domain and row tail only. Non-fixed structural changes recompute rows from the first regrouped row, and an actual lane-geometry change rebuilds at most all rows and cLane columns.
contract.adversarialWitness: Insert one item at index zero under a non-fixed size policy so every later dense row is regrouped, then change the effective viewport width so the lane count also changes; the repair visits at most nItem values and emits one replacement row set plus cLane columns.

fullScan.rationale: A lane-count change or a structural regrouping at the start can change every dense row aggregate; same-width frame-origin changes and bounded value windows do not take this full-rebuild branch.

variables.name: kPlacement
variables.meaning: placements emitted by the active Virtual plan

contract.proof: The shared Vue projector visits each emitted placement once, creates the native item VNode directly, and retains one element, registration disposer, and stable function ref per mounted identity. DOM owns item observation and measurement batching.
contract.adversarialWitness: A maximum render window mounts kPlacement distinct identities, then replaces the window so every cached registration is released and replaced without creating per-placement Sectile component instances.

fullScan.rationale: Projection work is bounded by emitted placements and may not traverse unmounted collection items.

operations.specificationCeiling: O(nItem log lLane + jChanged log nItem)

variables.name: jChanged
variables.meaning: changed collection identities or value-dependent extents

variables.name: lLane
variables.ceiling: lanePolicy fixed count or responsive maxCount

time.bound: O(nItem log lLane + jChanged log nItem)

assumptions: collection identity and changed-value windows come from the Virtual-owned projection
Masonry placement repair is owned by @sectile/virtual/masonry-layout
contract.proof: The Vue host performs no geometry work when the effective width and policy-derived lane geometry are unchanged. Structural and value changes are forwarded through Virtual-owned extent reconciliation. An actual lane geometry, itemGap, or placementPolicy change issues one Masonry geometry mutation; variable extents may then require the owner to rebuild every placement, while uniform extents remain formula-backed.
contract.adversarialWitness: Change the effective width under responsive lanes with variable extents and shortest-lane placement so the lane count changes and every item placement must be rebuilt; separately invalidate a changed value window near index zero so the owner must repair from the earliest affected item.

fullScan.rationale: A real lane-geometry or placement-policy change can observably change every Masonry placement; same-width frame-origin changes do not issue that mutation.

variables.name: jChanged
variables.meaning: changed collection/value window materialized by the Vue host

assumptions: collection identity and changed-value windows come from the Virtual-owned projection
packed Spatial geometry and repair are owned by @sectile/virtual/spatial-layout
contract.proof: Surface/frame changes are not reactive inputs to the Spatial state watcher and therefore issue no Spatial mutation. With stable geometry resolvers, the host materializes only the collection change window and, in mounted size ownership, performs StableID lookups only for that window to retain measured width and height. A getRect or getZIndex resolver identity change may affect every application rectangle and therefore materializes one full replacement.
contract.adversarialWitness: Replace the getRect resolver for an nItem collection so every declared rectangle may change; separately move the surface frame without changing collection values and assert the Spatial state identity and generation remain unchanged.

fullScan.rationale: Only an application resolver change may require a full host-side geometry replacement; frame movement and bounded stable-resolver updates do not take that branch.
